answer: Ferrous Epoch Clock: each agent identity must perform a small, unique proof-of-work tied to a slowly rotating ferrous token, so new identities cannot be mass-minted cheaply. Registration requires one prior voyage through a timed challenge round, delaying burst creation. Every identity's activity emits an echo hash chained to its epoch token, making cloned agents detectable and revocable. Attackers pay compute plus elapsed rounds per identity, so coordination itself becomes costly.
